claims.claim: The MT and Greek textual traditions diverge on Judah taking Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron, and Judges 1:19 does not erase the variant
claims.evidence: MT Judges 1:18 read in full (Hebrew + JPS English, Mechon Mamre): 'Judah took Gaza with its territory, and Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.' NETS Judges 1:18 in both recensions (A and B, read in full): 'And Ioudas did not inherit Gaza...' — the Greek adds Azotus (Ashdod) and reverses the outcome from capture to non-capture. Judges 1:19 limits Judah's success in the valley because of iron chariots; it says nothing about Gaza, Ashkelon or Ekron and erases neither reading. Do not harmonize the witnesses or claim all Greek manuscripts say precisely the same thing.

connections.note: Parallel Caleb, Achsah and Debir episode: Joshua 15:13–19 and Judges 1:10–15 preserve overlapping traditions about the same places. What they share is a literary relationship between texts; agreement among biblical passages is not equivalent to independent confirmation of the episodes.

Parallel west-Manasseh non-dispossession list: Joshua 17:11–13 lists Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach and Megiddo, and reports that the sons of Manasseh could not take possession of these cities but put the Canaanites to forced labor without driving them out completely — the same towns and the same outcome as Judges 1:27–28. Closely corresponding narrative subject, not archaeological corroboration.
Covenantal commands against assimilation and rival cults (Deuteronomy 7:1–6). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
A retrospective numerical chronology (1 Kings 6:1 gives an Exodus-to-temple figure), not independent proof; it does not directly describe events of Judges 1.
